issues.title: Unjustified cancellation in the linear-encoder proposition

diagnostic_evidence.quote: suppose that a linear encoder $\Psi'$ is injective on a linear subspace $V \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ with $\text{dim}(V)=n$.
It is always possible to decompose $f(p)$ into a contribution in $V$ and one in its orthogonal complement, i.e. $f(p) = f_V(p) + f_{V^\perp}(p)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Linearity gives $J_{\Psi'}f=J_{\Psi'}f_V+J_{\Psi'}f_{V^\perp}$. Injectivity of $J_{\Psi'}$ on $V$ does not imply that it annihilates $V^\perp$; for example, $(x,y)\mapsto x+y$ is injective on the $x$-axis but is nonzero on its orthogonal complement. Hence the asserted identity $F=J_{\Psi'}f_V$ does not follow from the stated assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the linear-encoder characterization fails, and that characterization cannot provide valid support for the later linear-encoder/nonlinear-decoder proposition without repair.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the argument with L = J_{Ψ′} and V = (ker L)⊥. Since L is injective on an n-dimensional subspace and has codomain R^n, it has rank n; hence L|V is an isomorphism and L annihilates V⊥ = ker L. The cancellation Lf = Lf_V is then valid for this canonically chosen V. Update the dependent proof to invoke this kernel-complement formulation rather than cancellation for an arbitrary V.
issues.why_classification: The cancellation is a genuine invalid inference, so it is not a typo. However, elementary rank-nullity and orthogonal-decomposition arguments repair the proposition and its use in the dependent result locally, without changing the encoder characterization or requiring new proof architecture.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: A linear encoder can only be injective on manifolds for which there exist both a linear subspace $V$ and a linear transformation $T:\mathcal{M}\to V$ such that $T$ is injective.

issues.title: Insufficiently explicit injectivity qualification in linear-encoder exactness proposition

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This requires that $\Psi\circ\Psi'$ is bijective and $\Psi'$ injective on $\mathcal{M}$

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition 4 states the decomposition f=f_V+f_(V-perp), which alone does not ensure exact reconstruction: two distinct manifold points can have the same retained component. However, Proposition 2 already explains that the retained component must be invertible on its image, and Proposition 4 directly cites it. The defect is the later statement's insufficiently explicit injectivity qualification, not absence of that condition or its explanation throughout the source.
issues.overall_effect: The formal proposition and its overview are unclear or misleading about the qualification needed for exact reconstruction. On the contextual reading supplied by the cited proposition, this does not establish failure of the intended injective-projection result or the absence of a substantial proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly require the retained projection f_V to be injective on the manifold, connect this requirement to Proposition 2, and make the same qualification clear in the overview. Define the decoder through the inverse on the projection's image. The intended latent dimension and zero-representation-error conclusion remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The necessary restriction is already explained in the directly referenced context. Making it explicit in the later proposition and overview is a short local formulation repair preserving the intended claim, rather than a newly imposed substantive restriction on the contextual model class. The decomposition alone remains insufficient, so the misleading formulation is retained as an issue.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: A linear--nonlinear autoencoder can reproduce a manifold $\mathcal{M}$ with $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ if there exist a linear space $V$ and a map $f_V$ such that the manifold is described by $f = f_V + f_{V^\perp}$ with $f_V$ injective.

issues.title: Unassumed Lipschitz constant in the reduced-field proposition

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Additionally, we assume that $F_N$ is bounded, with $M_{F_N} \coloneqq \sup_{u_N\in\mathcal{M}} \|F_N(u_N)\|$.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate of $F_n(u_{n1})-F_n(u_{n2})$ bounds the difference $F_N(\Psi(u_{n1}))-F_N(\Psi(u_{n2}))$ by $L_{F_N}\|\Psi(u_{n1})-\Psi(u_{n2})\|$. Boundedness of $F_N$ does not imply this inequality, and the old proposition never assumes that a finite $L_{F_N}$ exists.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed Lipschitz bound for $F_n$ and the later formal results using that finite constant are not established for a merely bounded $F_N$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In addition to boundedness, assume that F_N is Lipschitz on the relevant manifold or decoder image, with a finite constant L_{F_N}. Make every listed downstream result invoke this premise, or equivalently the resulting Lipschitz continuity of F_n. The displayed bound and all later stability, well-posedness, scaling, and convergence estimates then remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The proof explicitly uses L_{F_N}, so a real premise is missing and the defect is not typographical. Adding Lipschitz regularity is a short, standard, source-supported ODE regularity correction that preserves the method, conclusions, rates, and intended regular regime throughout the affected chain.

issues.title: Incorrect initial-perturbation aggregation for a nonlinear encoder

failure_location.quote: For simplicity, we sum the perturbations contribution, so we group them in a unique $\overline{\delta}_0 = \Psi'(\Delta_0) + \delta_0$, and $\overline{\delta} = J_{\Psi'}\Delta + \delta$, bounded by $\|\overline{\delta}_0\| < \eps_0$, with $\eps_0>0$, and $\|\overline{\delta}\| < \eps$, with $\eps>0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The perturbed initial value is $\Psi'(\ut_{N0}+\Delta_0)+\delta_0$, while the reference value is $\Psi'(\ut_{N0})$. Their difference is therefore $\Psi'(\ut_{N0}+\Delta_0)+\delta_0-\Psi'(\ut_{N0})$, not $\Psi'(\Delta_0)+\delta_0$ unless the encoder is linear and additive.
issues.overall_effect: The subsequent zero-stability estimate is stated for an incorrectly represented initial discrepancy when the encoder is nonlinear.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the definition by overline δ_0 = Ψ′(u_{N0}+Δ_0)+δ_0−Ψ′(u_{N0}). Then the rewritten initial condition is an identity; if an explicit bound is desired, use ‖overline δ_0‖ ≤ L_{Ψ′}‖Δ_0‖+‖δ_0‖. No subsequent estimate otherwise changes.
issues.why_classification: The perturbed and reference initial values displayed immediately around the definition uniquely force their difference. The later argument uses only this actual discrepancy and its norm, so correcting the malformed expression requires no choice, new inference, weakened guarantee, or reconstruction of the stability argument.

issues.title: Conditional absolute stability mislabeled as A-stability

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which leads to the well-known upper bound on the timestep size: $\max_i|1+\Delta t \lambda_i| < 1$, where $\lambda_i$ is the $i^{th}$ eigenvalue of $A$.

issues.failure_explanation: The heading and associated prose claim an analysis of preservation or enforcement of A-stability. The old body actually establishes conditions such as $|1+\Delta t\lambda_i|<1$ and a finite upper bound on $\Delta t$, which describe absolute or nonlinear stability for the specified problems. A-stability is an unconditional method property, so the old terminology materially overstates what the calculations establish.
issues.overall_effect: The stability calculations remain usable, but the headings and surrounding claims misrepresent conditional stability regions as the stronger method-level A- and B-stability properties.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rename the A-stability and weak B-stability discussions as linear absolute-stability and conditional nonlinear-stability analyses. State the Forward Euler inequalities and timestep bounds as conditional sufficient conditions for decay or contractivity, not as A-stability or B-stability of the method. The existing calculations and bounds can be retained.
issues.why_classification: The stronger A- and B-stability terminology makes a meaningful unconditional method-level promise, so withdrawing it is not a typo or a no-loss minor repair. However, the same model problems, schemes, stability regions, timestep bounds, and decay or contractivity conclusions survive as recognizably comparable conditional statements through a local reframing, avoiding both global reconstruction and major mathematical loss.
